name: five-minute-roundup
why: the reference format for plan.md §29.7 — every field in the schema appears here at least once, so a change to the spec that this file cannot express is a change somebody has to argue for

profile.why: at five minutes the choreography is 6% of the programme; default three-second seams across seven stories are 21 seconds, which is a whole story

source.why: the ranked homepage, already scored and clustered — this file shapes what it hands over and never reorders it

context.audience: a working software engineer, listening while doing something else
standing: assumes technical fluency — never explain what an API or a database is
this is the whole programme, not an excerpt from a longer one

never: never say 'more on that later' — at this length there is no later
never trail a story you are about to tell in the next sentence
always: name the publication once per story, and only once

never: never say the date more than once in the programme

program:end.direction: land it in one sentence and stop

never: never say 'welcome back' — nobody went anywhere

block:lead:begin.direction: open on the fact, not the setup

exceptions.why: 0.25 rather than the 0.35 a twelve-minute show can carry: at five minutes one boosted story is already a fifth of the programme and two would be the programme

rules.name: things you follow
rules.why: the ranker already put it in; this stops the format's own trimming demoting it to a namecheck

blocks.name: main
blocks.why: the only block with a target — a greeting, a lead and a sign-off have natural lengths no clock can stretch, so the body carries the fit and the rest are allowed for
